overview.short: Perched atop a 1,500-foot sheer cliff on the Kaimur plateau, Rohtasgarh is one of India’s largest and most formidable ancient hill fortresses, spanning 42 square kilometers.
overview.description: Commanding breathtaking panoramic views of the Son River valley, Rohtasgarh Fort was founded according to legend by Rohitashwa, son of King Harishchandra of Ayodhya. Strategically reinforced by Mughal general Raja Man Singh in the 16th century and captured by Sher Shah Suri in 1539, the immense fort complex encompasses royal palace quarters, the multi-storey Aina Mahal, intricate Hathiya Pol stone gates, Jami Masjid, Phulbari gardens, and hanging waterfalls cascading down the rugged Kaimur scarps.
features: Aina Mahal (Mirror Palace of Raja Man Singh)
overview.about: An adventurous trekker and history lover’s paradise where ancient stone arches, steep cliff faces, Mughal courtyards, and virgin jungle waterfalls meet on the Kaimur plateau.

howToReach.roadNote: Accessible via NH-19 (Grand Trunk Road) to Dehri-on-Sone or Sasaram, followed by SH-15 to Akbarpur base village.

topPlaces.name: Rohtasgarh Palace & Citadel Ramparts
topPlaces.description: Imposing stone palace citadel built by Raja Man Singh featuring royal darbar halls, residential quarters, hidden tunnels, and bastions overlooking the Son River.

image.alt: Rohtasgarh Palace & Citadel Ramparts in Rohtasgarh Fort, Bihar

topPlaces.name: Aina Mahal (Mirror Palace of Raja Man Singh)
topPlaces.description: Three-storey sandstone pleasure pavilion adorned with carved jharokhas, cupolas, and ornamental plasterwork, which served as the Mughal governor’s headquarters.

image.alt: Aina Mahal (Mirror Palace of Raja Man Singh) in Rohtasgarh Fort, Bihar

topPlaces.name: Hathiya Pol (Monumental Elephant Gateway)
topPlaces.description: Main royal portal erected in 1597 flanked by life-sized stone elephant sculptures, guard chambers, and formidable arrow slits.

image.alt: Hathiya Pol (Monumental Elephant Gateway) in Rohtasgarh Fort, Bihar

topPlaces.name: Jami Masjid of Rohtasgarh
topPlaces.description: Grand 1543 white-plastered stone mosque built during the reign of Sher Shah Suri, featuring three domed bays, arched arcades, and a spacious prayer courtyard.

image.alt: Jami Masjid of Rohtasgarh in Rohtasgarh Fort, Bihar

topPlaces.name: Chaurasan Mandir & Rohitaswa Temple
topPlaces.description: Historic hilltop temple complex with 84 steps dedicated to Lord Shiva and King Rohitashwa, commanding panoramic views of the forested ravines.

image.alt: Chaurasan Mandir & Rohitaswa Temple in Rohtasgarh Fort, Bihar

topPlaces.name: Phulwari Bagh (Royal Mughal Gardens)
topPlaces.description: Symmetrical Charbagh-style terraced pleasure garden complex featuring stone water channels, ornamental fountains, and pavilion ruins.

faq.q: How physically demanding is the trek to Rohtasgarh Fort?
faq.a: The uphill trek from Akbarpur base takes 2 to 3 hours along a stepped stone path. Moderate fitness is recommended. Carry plenty of water.

faq.q: Is it safe to visit Rohtasgarh Fort with family?
faq.a: Yes, daytime visits are very popular and safe, especially on weekends between October and March.

faq.q: Are guides available at the fort base?
faq.a: Local village guides are readily available at Akbarpur base to assist with navigation and narrate historical legends.
